what: std-hello stopped at `init::reset_sigpipe`: `mod sigpipe` in a #[cfg] block 'that a macro call wrote or that is in a local item's body'. The refusal's words name two causes; the real one was the second: reset_sigpipe is a fn declared inside `init`'s body, and the names library never wrote block modules for a local fn's body (the scan does not read inside items, and front2's library_body gave None for any local item).
cost: about fifteen minutes to see that the fn is local (the refusal names `init::reset_sigpipe` as if it were a module item)
cause: a block was written as a module only for items that make one or statement calls directly in it; a local fn whose own body needs modules left nothing for it
whys: the library keyed block modules by the library item whose body it is; a local fn had no library key, so its body could have none
class: any struct, enum, union, alias, trait, mod, extern crate, impl or statement call in the body of a fn, const or static that is itself declared in a body
prevention: done: NestedItem::body_writes (the scan reads one bit from a local item's own text, recursively), so its block is written and the fn is a module item with the library's key; front2 Locals::library_twin finds that key; one library_body for Locals::keep and PatternBlocks::of
annoyance: the refusal 'a mod in a block that a macro call wrote or that is in a local item's body' names two causes and the path `init::reset_sigpipe` hides that the fn is local
workaround: read the pinned std source at the line the refusal names
